title: League Parity Index
headline_insight: The NBA drifted slightly less balanced across three seasons: the win-share Gini rose from 0.177 in 2023-24 to 0.2004 in 2025-26.
what_it_means: Even at the top of that range the league is very balanced (0 is perfectly even), so the shift is small. Roughly a quarter of games are decided by 5 points or fewer, edging up from 23.3% to 25.5%, and the average absolute final margin sits around 12.6 to 13.0 points.
how_to_read: Each season's win concentration is summarized by a Gini of team win shares (lower is more balanced) plus close-game share and margin dispersion.
why_it_matters: It is a descriptive read on competitive balance over time, a companion to strength-of-schedule work rather than a forecast.
caveat: NOT a forecast of any future season; NOT strength-of-schedule adjusted (opponent-raw win counts); pooled with any playoff games in the parquet, which inflate win concentration. The 2024-25 and 2025-26 rows are flagged as looking partial versus a full 1230-game season.
